title: Health Holder

contributors.contribution: Provided the dietary methodology and nutrition-domain requirements that I translated into the application.

description: I worked with a nutritionist to turn her dietary program into a Java desktop application built on my Hydra-Gen application engine. Health Holder tracked food-group targets and detailed nutritional values, supported daily meal and exercise scheduling, and provided status and charting tools to help users monitor their progress.

sections.title: Nutrition Tracking
paragraphs: I translated the nutritionist's dietary system into a structured application that tracked both food-group targets and detailed nutritional information.
Users could monitor values such as calories, fat, cholesterol, sodium, carbohydrates, fibre, sugar, protein, vitamins, and minerals.

sections.title: Food & Nutrient Model
paragraphs: The application used structured domain objects for foods, portions, food groups, nutrient definitions, time periods, schedules, and daily reports.
Food records supported serving conversions such as cups, grams, and ounces together with food-group and nutrient values.

sections.title: Meal & Exercise Scheduling
paragraphs: Users could plan meals and exercise across daily and weekly schedules rather than simply recording food after it had been consumed.
The application organized activity into configurable time slots and day-based schedules.

sections.title: Progress & Reporting
paragraphs: Health Holder included status and reporting views that helped users compare their activity and nutrition against their targets.
The interface also included charting and daily-report functionality for reviewing progress.

sections.title: Built with Hydra-Gen
paragraphs: I built Health Holder on my Hydra-Gen application engine rather than creating an unrelated one-off Java UI.

The application used Hydra-Gen's reusable widget, navigation, session, display, and XML infrastructure, demonstrating that the platform could support applications well outside its original educational-software domain.

sections.title: Reusable Application Components
paragraphs: Health Holder was assembled from application-specific widgets and views layered on top of Hydra-Gen.
Examples included food entry, food search, calorie tracking, eating-time configuration, schedule editing, food-group displays, information views, and today's-status views.

sections.title: Working with a Domain Expert
paragraphs: The project required turning a specialist's existing dietary methodology into software concepts, data structures, workflows, and user interfaces.
That made Health Holder as much a requirements-and-domain-modeling project as a programming exercise.

historicalNotes: Health Holder was developed in Java in collaboration with a nutritionist whose dietary methodology formed the application's domain requirements.
The original legacy card identified Java 1.2.
Surviving source confirms that Health Holder was built directly on the Hydra-Gen application engine.
Health Holder imports and uses Hydra-Gen session, widget, display, navigation, and XML infrastructure.
This is direct surviving-code evidence that Hydra-Gen was a general-purpose application platform rather than being limited to educational applications.
Health Holder contains application-specific widgets including AddFoodWidget, CaloriesWidget, EatTimesWidget, EditSlotWidget, FindFoodWidget, GroupsWidget, InfoWidget, ScheduleWidget, and TodayWidget.
The domain model includes FoodItem, Facts, Portion, Groups, GroupDefinition, NutrientDefinition, TimeDefinition, TimeSlot, Day, and DayReport structures.
FoodItem supports portion conversions including cups, grams, and ounces together with nutritional and food-group values.
JavaZoom/JLayer source is present alongside the Hydra-Gen runtime used by Health Holder.
Hydra-Gen contains Hydra-specific JLayer integration classes including HydraDecoder, HydraAdvancedPlayer, and HydraSoundAudioDevice.
The JavaZoom/JLayer integration should be treated as Hydra-Gen's shared audio/playback infrastructure rather than as a Health Holder-specific technology.
Hydra-Gen's shared audio subsystem could therefore be inherited by applications across the platform, including the 60+ educational programs that required speech, music, sound effects, or other audio.
The Spelling List Editor had additional recording requirements, but the surviving evidence does not establish that it was the original reason JavaZoom/JLayer was integrated.
Do not list JavaZoom/JLayer as a headline Health Holder technology unless future source archaeology shows that Health Holder itself actively used audio.
